tasks.title: Wavelength in water. (6p)
tasks.statement:
Determine the wavelength of the radio waves in water.
You may use the setup shown in Figure 2.

lems Text for Student: COM-A1

    In the following tasks you will study the propagation
  of waves in metallic tubes ﬁlled with medium (water or
  air) in which case

                     ⃗ 0 (r, ϕ)e−αz ei(kz−ωt) ,

                  E                                       (1)

  where E ⃗ stands for the electric ﬁeld vector, α describes
  the attenuation due to dissipation in the medium (for
  water α > 0, for air α = 0), and we have used cylindrical
  coordinates r, ϕ, z.
    The function E   ⃗ 0 (r, ϕ) represents a standing wave
  across the cross-section of the waveguide. Different
  standing waves in the cross-section correspond to dif-
  ferent propagation modes of the wave in the waveguide.
  The dispersion relation for the waves in a waveguide is
  given by
                         ω 2 = (k⋆2 + k 2 ) c2 ,          (2)

  where c is the speed of light in the medium ﬁlling the

  waveguide, and k⋆ is a positive constant depending only

  on the diameter of the tube and on the propagation

  mode. In your experiment, all the other propagation

  modes except for the mode with the smallest value of

  k⋆ can be ignored. Pay attention to the fact that a wave

  can propagate along the waveguide without attenuation

  (with a real-valued wave vector k) only if the oscillation

  frequency is high enough, ω ≥ ck⋆ . Equations (1) and (2)

  remain valid for lower frequencies yielding purely imag-

  inary k = iµ which corresponds to a decaying (evanes-

  cent) mode.

tasks.title: a. Decaying modes in air-filled waveguides
tasks.statement:
(2p) Put the emitter into the aluminium tube of diame-
  ter d1 = 46 mm and study how the power P of the waves
  received by the receiver at the outlet of the tube depends
  on the distance z of the emitter from the outlet of the
  tube. From the measurement of P as a function of z
  determine the value of the parameter µ of the decaying
  mode.
